commits.summary: Draft the application-core loop: four streams that widen native change verification to ordinary service code
commits.body:
Adds llm-dlc/loops/application-core.md, its four stream briefs (objects, values, environment, reuse) and application-core-acceptance.md, adapted from an outside plan the user shared (a review of the repository at cbf183a on GitHub). Each of the review's claims about the code was recounted at wwlnosom (20f1a17d), with file:line evidence, in the main brief's 'Where it starts from'. All held, and one sharpened: ObjectDomain's made_by, classes, allocations and label are read by nothing outside the cache key's projection, so Phase 0's first step is a gate that refuses them. The briefs follow brief-template.md: the cleanup run's pipeline mode, the timebox, application-core-STREAM workspaces, reserved example ranges 230-279, 4 GB scopes, fresh session ids, and the planning session 3da21514 as the fork. Shared files get a single writer (Phase 0, before the fork), because the foundations and cleanup integration checks both stopped on merge conflicts. The six decisions are proposed, not yet settled by the user.

Also registers the names application-core and application-core-STREAM in feature-loop.sh (refusing application-core-acceptance, which is not a brief), and application-core with its four streams in run-streams.sh. Adds llm-dlc/tools/application-core-integration.sh, which tells a compile failure, a failure of the integration contract lib/tests/application_core.rs (written in Phase 0) and other test failures apart. Both scripts were replaced by rename, because run-streams.sh cleanup was running from this workspace and bash reads a running script incrementally. Checked with bash -n and by resolving the four names through feature-loop.sh's case. Not launched: the cleanup merge, Phase 0 and the user's decisions come first.

commits.summary: Record verification results for 3 jobs: VF-021 closed, VF-014's fresh benchmark recorded
commits.body: On vm-1: the fresh lib/benchmark results (job 20261107-183709, 1h37m, peak 6.0 GiB of an estimated 4.5) passed and replaced results.json and RESULTS.md; the VF-010 comparison (job 20261107-184603) passed with 557 own-checker runs, verdicts changed 0, closing VF-021; the VF-014 comparison from earlier is recorded. Verified by the jobs' logs and collect's apply with no conflicts.

commits.summary: Loops print their session when they end
commits.body: feature-loop.sh logs 'session: ID' from its EXIT trap, so the session to resume or read is the last line however the loop ended: done, out of cycles, no commit, an error or Ctrl-C. run-streams.sh logs, after its final status, the planning session, the merge loop's session (the main brief's, or FEATURE_LOOP_SESSION) and each stream's. The integration check is a script and has no session. Both scripts were replaced by rename, since run-streams.sh cleanup is still running from this workspace on the old copy, which therefore won't print them; checked with bash -n.

commits.summary: run-streams.sh reads only job-id-shaped words from a 'waiting on jobs' status
commits.body: The cleanup-jbmc stream ended its Progress with 'Status: waiting on jobs ID 20261107-...', copying the template's literal ID. run-streams.sh took every word after 'waiting on jobs' as a job id, so it waited for verification/results/ID*/result.json, which never comes. All nine real jobs were collected by about 18:00, and the stream sat waiting from 17:31 toward the 12-hour RUN_STREAMS_JOB_WAIT. A new job_ids keeps only words shaped like an id (YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS...), and both places that parse the status use it. Tested on that status line, and on an empty one; bash -n. Replaced by rename: the run under way keeps the old copy, so it stays stuck until it is restarted.

commits.summary: Draft the stub-reachability brief: decide by the solver whether a proof enters a JBMC stub (settles VF-015)
commits.body: VF-015's step 3 (prove Hex#toDigit under ch == 1632) fails only because the gap preflight counts String.format's stub as entered. Its symbolic run (--program-only, no solver) can't prune a branch an --assume decides, and that call is on toDigit's exception path, infeasible there. The user chose a solver check of stub reachability over a String.format model: under --no-refine-strings JBMC can't read a format string, so a model would be unsound or a source of spurious refutations. The brief runs after the cleanup merge, since jbmc_gaps.rs is the cleanup jbmc stream's file. Its steps: an experiment job comparing --cover location with an alternative on VF-015's harness; choose the method; implement it as a third preflight step with recorded-output unit tests; resubmit VF-015 unchanged as N3's second attempt, with guard jobs. Status blocked on the merge; nothing run yet.

commits.summary: VF-009 and VF-019 closed by their checks; VF-018 and VF-001 deferred to the user: three of heap's JBMC tests time out at 1800 s, and VF-001's jobs fail on their own tee
commits.body:
The cleanup-jbmc stream read its nine collected jobs. VF-009's check (20261107-172721-jbmc-s-extra-initializers-named-and-refu, step 2) passed: under auto --confirm, boomTwice and enumBroken are NoVerdict with the own checker's Verified standing, under strict and assume. VF-019's (20261107-172721-nullable-and-one-array-parameters-in-pro) passed, with the six claims refused by name. Both entries can be closed. The measurement 20261107-171442 shows that throwing-initializer refuses none of the 41 recorded JBMC examples' 43 obligations: the only refusal at a JBMC defect is 037#0, the existing unmasked-shift guard.

VF-018: with JVMCONTRACT_HEAP_TIME_LIMIT=1800, Prices#total passed (20261107-164356-vf-018-prices-...), and Kernel#price, Lines#reprice and Orders#reprice still timed out on their first JBMC run. By decision 6 it is deferred to the user, with no second attempt. Progress records how long each ran and a look at the harness: 14 to 17 lines, two or three primitive inputs, no loops. In each, what is left to prove is the equality of two separately built 64-bit products of symbolic operands, which the own checker proves in under 0.1 s.

VF-001: in 20261107-172721-conformance-corpus-under-jbmc-and-engine, both ignored conformance tests pass (2 passed, 0 failed), but the step exits 1. Its command pipes into 'tee target/conformance-jbmc.log' under pipefail, and lib/target/ does not exist yet when tee opens it in the job's fresh work directory. The original 20261106-021741 and -024336 runs show the same tee error, so these jobs can't pass as written. The sibling was stopped by SIGTERM in the runner's scope-name collision (VF-021, fixed in wwlnosom). The brief forbids rewriting a check, so the user decides whether to take that job's test result as the check, or to resubmit both with mkdir -p target added.

Only the brief's Progress changed. Out of date elsewhere: jbmc-upstream.md's 'Where it starts from' and Deferred sections still call VF-009 untriaged, which is outside the candidate reports this stream may edit. Seen, not taken: the native stream's VF-015 now needs a String.format model in lib/models/ (this stream's file, not its item), and the integration check's conflict is only in generated files (llm-dlc/README.md, index.json, traces/).
The cleanup-jbmc stream's last turns, recorded by the cleanup reconcile before the merge. No code changes.

commits.summary: VF-014 closed by the isolated comparison, and the fresh lib/benchmark/results.json applied on the default line: the examples stream is done
commits.body:
Both of E2's jobs passed and were collected in the default workspace (lmxwvplz). 20261107-183328-vf-014-h1-isolated-run-3-of-3-the-benchm compared H1's own-checker runs with H1's parent's: 557 runs, 24 new (the swaps cases H1 added), 0 verdicts changed, 0 formulas grown, 0 paths or merges changed. So H1 changed no verdict, and the 8 changed verdicts of 20261107-041414 came from the stale recording. The verification loop closed VF-014 in findings.md.

20261107-183709-vf-014-a-fresh-lib-benchmark-results-jso recorded native, jbmc and auto under every mode and staging policy in 1h37m, with no false success or alarm, and collect applied results.json and RESULTS.md: 2829 runs against the old file's 1802. Its 6.0 GiB peak was at its limit, so the Progress suggests a bigger budget for the next full recording. This branch doesn't touch results.json, so the merge takes the new one.

Verified by reading both jobs' reports (pipeline.py report) and the run counts of the applied results.json. Every item is now closed by its check or deferred by the timebox (VF-002's 147 and 148), so the brief's status is done. This cycle's prompt again named the default workspace's copy of the brief, whose Progress predates this stream; this workspace's copy is the one updated.
The cleanup-examples stream's last turns, recorded by the cleanup reconcile before the merge. No code changes.

commits.summary: N1 done: VF-010's benchmark comparison passed, and N3 (VF-015) blocked on the user's decision
commits.body:
Job 20261107-184603-vf-010-s-benchmark-compared-the-own-chec passed on vm-1. It compared the own checker's 557 benchmark runs at the VF-010 fix (f606b0d8) and at its parent (c307e721), and found 0 verdicts changed, 0 cases new or gone, 0 formulas grown past 10%, and 0 paths or merges changed. The verification agent closed VF-021 with it, and VF-010 was already closed, so the stream's N1 is finished. N2 (VF-011) passed its check earlier and is done here; findings.md still lists it as open until the verification agent records it.

N3 (VF-015, example 109) can't pass without the user. Its last run failed at step 3 because strict mode refuses JBMC's proof, which reaches JBMC's stub of String.format, not at the witness replay. Following the main brief, a check that can't pass for a reason outside the item is deferred to the user rather than rewritten. Either the user allows --gaps assume or advised for step 3, or the jbmc stream adds a String.format model. Only the stream brief's Progress changed, and its status is now blocked. Nothing to compile or test.
The cleanup-native stream's last turns, recorded by the cleanup reconcile before the merge. No code changes.

commits.summary: Merge the three cleanup streams: native, jbmc and examples
commits.body:
The reconcile of llm-dlc/loops/cleanup.md (Phase 4, step 1). All three streams had stopped: native blocked on VF-015, jbmc blocked on VF-018 and VF-001 (both for the user), examples done. Each stream's last turns were recorded on its branch, their logs and run records copied into the default workspace, and the three branches merged with the default line. The workspaces cleanup-native, cleanup-jbmc, cleanup-examples and cleanup-integration are forgotten; their directories stay on disk for the user to delete.

Conflicts: only the generated trace files (llm-dlc/index.json, llm-dlc/traces/README.md, llm-dlc/traces/metrics.json, regenerated by this commit) and llm-dlc/README.md, where the default line's application-core sentences and the examples stream's run-record paragraph (VF-013) are both kept. The other files two lines changed (lib/src/equivalence.rs, lib/tests/heap.rs, lib/README.md, examples/index.json) merged cleanly, with independent edits. build.py --index-only marks example 149's page current, since its job passed.

Verified inline at the merge: the lib unit tests (210) and every test binary except integration.rs pass: alignment 34, compare 1, conformance 10 (2 JBMC tests ignored), effects 17, foundations 5 (the integration contract), heap 47 (9 JBMC tests ignored), observations 12, skill 1, summaries 40. integration.rs is left out because its non-ignored tests run JBMC; Phase 4's rerun job runs it at the merge. Every Python suite passes (examples/tools, lib/benchmark, lib/solvers, llm-dlc/tools, verification). test_performance.py failed one test once while cargo was loading the machine, and passed when rerun alone; its output was not kept.

The brief's Progress folds the streams' work: the timebox's one deferral (VF-002's 147 and 148), the three items deferred to the user (VF-018, VF-001, VF-015), and each entry's closing job. Next: step 2, the run records this commit publishes for the first time, then step 3's rerun of the merge's examples.

Out of date in the rest of the brief: 'Where it starts from' describes the state before the streams. VF-015 is no longer the native stream's open item: the user chose llm-dlc/loops/stub-reachability.md (rmvlorrs) to close it after this merge.
